checks: Norm-one zeta of exact odd order m exists because m divides q+1. X cyclic shift and Y clock preserve the displayed standard Hermitian form. Oddness gives detX=1 and detY=zeta^(m(m-1)/2)=1 also in characteristic2.
X^a Y^b is scalar only for a=b=0 modulo m, by coordinate-line permutation and the first two diagonal entries. Thus the projective image is exactly (Z/m)^2, inside the stated natural PSU image.
The relation XY=zeta^(-1)YX gives the cocycle c((a,b),(a2,b2))=zeta^(b*a2). Because X^m=Y^m=1, reduction of exponents adds no cocycle. Its mth power is pointwise1.

Every trivial-action coboundary on an abelian group is symmetric. The alternating ratio on the two basis elements is zeta^(-1); hence every annihilating exponent is divisible by m. This proves exact order in K^times itself, without assuming injection from mu_m.
Restriction of the full semilinear scalar extension to trivial field character is the ordinary extension, so the same obstruction applies.

For p=2 the choices m=2^f+1 are odd and unbounded. For odd p and positive even f, p^f is1 modulo8, so m=(p^f+1)/2 is odd and unbounded. Retaining m>=5 lies in the already recognized simple unitary ranges.

The result excludes only a uniform algebraic scalar-exponent argument based on the natural unitary form. It supplies no maps from a fixed geometric group and no geometric Brauer-period lower bound, no counterexample to the open counting theorem, and no main movement.
